text: Social media feed
Picks which posts to show you first.
It learned from what millions of people liked and watched, then guesses what you will tap.
Face filter
Puts puppy ears on your selfie.
It learned from many face photos where eyes and noses are, even when you move.
Symptom-checker app
You type how you feel and it suggests what it might be.
It guesses from patterns in past cases. It is only a guess, so a health worker decides.
Maps traffic guess
Says your trip will take 20 minutes.
It guesses from patterns in past traffic. A guess, not a promise.
Spam filter
Moves junk email to a separate folder.
It learned from many junk and normal messages what spam usually looks like.
Voice assistant
You say "call Mom" and it dials.
It learned from many recorded voices how to turn sound into words.
Photo app that groups faces
Puts every photo of Lola in one album.
It learned to match faces from many examples.
Auto-captions on a video
Words appear on screen as people talk.
It learned from hours of speech to guess the words, and sometimes guesses wrong.
Translation app
Turns Tagalog into English as you type.
It learned patterns from huge amounts of text that was already translated.
"You may also like" list
Suggests things after you buy something.
It guesses from patterns in what other shoppers bought together.
Bank alert for odd card use
Texts you when a payment looks strange.
It learned what normal spending looks like and flags what does not fit.
Chatbot that writes its own replies
Answers questions you type in a chat box.
It learned patterns from lots of text and guesses the next words. It can sound sure and still be wrong.
Phone keyboard suggestions
Offers the next word as you type.
It learned which words usually follow each other.
X-ray reading helper
Marks spots on an X-ray for a doctor to check.
It learned from many X-rays. It helps, but the doctor decides.
Pocket calculator
Adds, subtracts and multiplies.
It follows fixed rules. Same input, same answer, no learning.
Rice-cooker timer
Cooks for 30 minutes, then clicks off.
A fixed countdown. It does not guess anything.
Light switch
On or off.
Nothing is guessed. You flip it and it obeys.
TV remote
Changes the channel when you press a button.
Each button sends one fixed signal. Nothing is learned.
Alarm clock
Rings at 6:00 every morning.
It rings at the time you set. No patterns, no guessing.
Three-speed electric fan
Low, medium or high.
A switch picks a fixed speed. The fan does not decide anything.
Traffic light on a timer
Changes colour every 60 seconds.
It follows a fixed schedule and does not look at the traffic.
Digital thermometer
Shows your body temperature.
A sensor measures and shows the number. It is not guessing from patterns.
Doorbell
Rings when someone presses it.
Press, ring. A fixed rule with nothing to learn.
Flashlight
Shines when you slide the switch.
A battery, a bulb and a switch. No learning inside.
Herbal tea
The box says it "cleans your blood" with an AI-made formula.
Hype alert! "AI-powered" is a sticker, not proof. It is tea in a bag, and no tea cleans your blood.
AI-powered!
Vitamin gummies
The label says AI picked the perfect formula for you.
Hype alert! Every buyer gets the same gummy. Nothing inside learns about you.
AI-formulated!
Energy bracelet
An ad says it balances your energy using AI.
Hype alert! It is a plain bracelet with no learning inside. A sticker does not make it AI.
Powered by AI!
Sugar-lowering pill
A post says it lowers blood sugar in three days.
Hype alert! Adding "AI" proves nothing. Check the FDA and ask a health worker first.

How long should I wash my hands?
Wet your hands, lather with soap, and scrub the front, back, between the fingers and under the nails for at least 20 seconds. Rinse with clean water and dry with a clean towel.
A general, well-known answer. It does not claim anything about you.
This one is already good. It is plain, general and easy to check at your health center.
WHO hand hygiene guidance (20 seconds with soap and water)
What is ORS, the oral rehydration salts my nurse mentioned?

ORS is a packet of salts and sugar that you mix with clean water. It replaces the water and salts the body loses with diarrhoea. Mix it exactly the way the packet says. If the diarrhoea does not stop, or there is blood, please see a health worker.
It explains what ORS is, follows the packet, and points to a health worker when things do not improve.
Keep it general: what ORS does, to follow the packet, and when to see a health worker.
WHO and DOH oral rehydration guidance
Why do children need vaccines?

Vaccines teach the body to recognise certain germs before a real infection. They are tested for safety before approval and monitored afterwards. Ask your barangay health center for your child's vaccine schedule.
A well-established fact, said calmly, with a pointer to the health center.
It would say just this: how vaccines work, that safety is checked, and where to get the schedule.
WHO and DOH immunization information
What do the two numbers in a blood pressure reading mean?

Blood pressure is the force of blood against the walls of your arteries. The top number is the pressure when the heart beats and the bottom number is the pressure between beats. High blood pressure often has no signs, so regular checks at the health center help. Ask a health worker what your numbers mean for you.
It explains the words in a general way and sends you to a health worker for your own numbers.
Explain the words, then say that your own numbers are for a health worker to read.
WHO hypertension fact sheet
How do I stop mosquitoes from breeding around our house?

The Aedes mosquito that spreads dengue breeds in clean standing water. Cover, clean and empty drums, cans, tires and flower pot trays every week. Wear long sleeves and use repellent, and see a health worker early if someone has a fever.
This matches the DOH 4S advice: search and destroy breeding places, protect yourself, and seek early consultation.
